scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

estimate substitution when no accepted read

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-03.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

H-REQUESTER-FRAME.statement: Dispute surge due to incorrect bills needing AI agent to auto-answer and fix root cause.

H-RULE-CHANGE-IMPACT.statement: Recent changes to billing import validation rules introduced defects that mis-map reads to bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Dispute ticket volume rose from ~610 in June and 590 in July to 1180 in August and 1260 in September, indicating roughly a doubling since August relative to the pre‑August baseline.
The observation shows 1,240 disputed bills with ESTIMATED reads and 1,785 with ACTUAL reads, indicating that disputes are not limited to estimate substitution.
Route completion for Aug‑Sep is 0.88 (88%) against a target of 0.95, with 9,200 manual read accounts, indicating field meter‑reading coverage is below target.
The tariff change log shows no records, indicating no tariff changes were made during the period.

E-05.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Staffing shortage of three field readers since July causes delayed manual meter reads, leading to estimate substitution and potentially higher dispute bills.
The CRM shows dispute tickets are being answered within the SLA, with a median response of 1.6 days and a total of 2,440 tickets in the period.

E-07.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The stakeholder states that there has been no tariff change this year, indicating that tariff modifications are not a source of the recent billing dispute increase.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The service contract clause shows that any route priority change must be confirmed by the Field Operations Manager, indicating that route‑based solutions are contingent on this approval step. It does not speak to the cause of disputed bills.

U-U1.question: What proportion of disputes is attributable to estimate substitution versus errors on actual reads?
U-U1.resolution_path: Analyze disputed bills by read type to quantify proportion attributable to estimate substitution vs actual-read errors.
U-U1.safe_placeholder: Proceed with route completion and estimate logic improvements while awaiting proportion analysis.

U-U2.question: Is staffing shortage the primary driver of delayed reads, or are routing/scheduling inefficiencies dominant?
U-U2.resolution_path: Investigate whether staffing shortage or routing/scheduling inefficiencies are the primary driver of delayed reads via time‑motion study and route efficiency analysis.
U-U2.safe_placeholder: Implement route scheduling optimizations and monitor completion; defer headcount increase decision until analysis complete.

U-U3.question: Does MDMS read latency contribute materially to estimate substitution?
U-U3.resolution_path: Measure MDMS read latency and correlate with estimate substitution frequency.
U-U3.safe_placeholder: Advance estimate substitution logic updates assuming low latency impact; monitor latency metrics.
